Basic information.Title: Reading clubs start a new term
Basic information.Excerpt: After-school reading sessions return, with new books for every reading level.

Body.text: Our after-school reading clubs are back for a new term. Children meet twice a week to read together, borrow books to take home and build the confidence that comes with reading for pleasure.
This term the clubs have new books for every level, from first picture books to short novels, and volunteers on hand to listen to every reader.

Basic information.Title: Why we start by listening
Basic information.Excerpt: On letting communities set the priorities — and why it makes the work last.
Basic information.Author: ⚠ Rising Beyond Borders (proposed; the website shows no author — use the real author's name, with consent, or leave empty)

Body.text: Every piece of work we do begins with a conversation. Before any plan or budget, we ask the people closest to a challenge what they need, what is already working and what a good result would look like to them.
It is slower at the start. But work shaped by the people it serves is work they own — and work people own is work that lasts after any single project ends.
Listening does not stop once a project begins. We keep asking, keep adjusting, and report back on what we heard.
